items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: I see this sign, “Bop City.” Doug Duke at the organ, the George Shearing Quintet, and Lionel Hampton and his Orchestra.

ctx.x: And you happened to see Lionel Hampton?

Yes. We flew over on BOAC and we got behind. And consequently they put us up at the Gotham Hotel, 55th and Fifth Avenue. They don’t do that anymore. And I had never been to North America. All I could remember in my lifetime is rationing, you couldn’t buy clothes, couldn’t buy candies, you only got an ounce and a quarter of meat a week or something or other, it was pretty bad. And when I got this offer from the same chap, I say, “Oh boy, you play the bloody drums?” He wrote me this letter, because we didn’t have a…

there at the time. I remember once I went in and there was a brand new set of Slingerland drums with big cymbals. I couldn’t believe it. I thought jeez, I’ve got to get to America, I’ve really got to get to America. Anyway, this night we were playing this aerodrome — and it was a very large aerodrome. And this guy came up, and I was playing drums in this accordion band, and this guy came up with a little tiny vibraphone and he starts to tap with one hand and he had a flatbed guitar and he’d put an electric motor…
